fix(pwa): prevent redirected navigation failures

Closes #46

## Root cause
Cloudflare Pages redirects `/index.html` to `/` with HTTP 308. The service worker precached that redirected response and served it for navigation, which Chrome rejects from a `FetchEvent` and surfaces as `ERR_FAILED`.

## Fix
- Precache the non-redirected root shell (`/`) only.
- Resolve navigation and static assets from the active versioned cache instead of a global cache lookup.
- Pin the non-redirected-shell contract with a regression test.

## Verification
- `npm --prefix app test -- --run src/pwa/pwa.test.ts` — 6 passed.
- `npm --prefix app test -- --run` — 67 passed.
- `npm --prefix app run typecheck` — passed.
- `npm --prefix app run build` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

## Rollback
Revert this merge commit if offline navigation regresses.

Addons: Reduce a11y report size and retention in Vitest

Refs #36124

## What I did

Storybook’s test-runner parent kept a11y reports from previous runs. Execa stored incoming IPC messages even after Storybook had handled them. Repeating tests left more reports in memory.

This PR disables that message history with `buffer: { ipc: false }`. Storybook still receives live messages, and stdout/stderr remain available.

For standalone Vitest, the `afterEach` hook defaults axe’s `resultTypes` to `['violations', 'incomplete']` when no value is set. This keeps full violation and incomplete results while limiting passing and inapplicable results to at most one node per rule.

The hook passes these options to the shared a11y runner. Manual checks keep their existing behavior. Explicit `resultTypes` settings, including an empty array, take precedence. Storybook UI reports keep their full results by default.

### Before and after

With 600 stories and a 768 MiB parent heap limit, the original runner ran out of memory while receiving the third run’s results. With IPC buffering disabled, all five runs completed.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parent heap after GC | 352 → 684 MiB, then OOM during run 3 | 319.54–320.16 MiB across 5 runs |
| IPC messages retained after a separate 30-story × 3-run check | 79, including reports from all 3 runs | 0; all 79 messages still received |
| Report size in a separate 200-row fixture | 1,150,644 bytes | 48,248 bytes; violation and incomplete content preserved |

The repeated-run comparison used synthetic stories, real Chromium tests and Storybook’s production child runner. Only IPC buffering differed between the two runs. The full manager UI was not included.

These results show that disabling IPC history removes the report accumulation observed in the Storybook parent. The reporter’s exact command and rerun workflow are still unknown, and our standalone CLI checks did not reproduce their OOM. This PR therefore uses **Refs #36124** until the fix can be checked against that workflow.

<details>
<summary>Test environments and additional measurements</summary>

These are synthetic HTML stories running real Chromium, axe, Vitest and the production Storybook child-runner code. The driver exercises the parent/child store path without the full manager UI. Before/after pairs use the same stories and full a11y reports; the only behavior changed in these pairs is IPC buffering. Values below are parent JS heap after GC, in MiB.

| Environment | Before | With IPC buffering disabled |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PR checkout `44938d86a87`, Storybook 11.0.0-alpha.3, Node 24.3.0; 600 stories/run; 768 MiB parent limit | 352.32 → 684.05; OOM receiving run 3 results after its 600 tests passed | 600 tests passed in each of 5 completed runs; 319.54 → 320.16 |
| Published 10.5.7, Node 25.9.0; 30 stories × 3; 768 MiB limit | 167.57 → 311.47 → 446.84 | 56.37 → 74.71 → 57.65; all tests passed |
| Published 10.5.10, Node 25.9.0; 30 stories × 3; 768 MiB limit | 100.16 → 192.71 → 276.54 | 60.88 → 58.78 → 56.40; all tests passed |
| Published 10.5.10, Node 25.9.0; 600 stories/run; 6144 MiB limit | 600 tests passed, then parent OOM before the first completed-run sample | 4 runs completed; 614.76 → 614.90 → 615.05 → 615.12. Run 5 was interrupted by the experiment's overall 30-minute limit |

### Standalone Vitest checks

All CLI runs below completed without OOM, using default concurrency and no forced GC between runs.

| Storybook | Execution | Completed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10.5.10 | Browser tests; `r` key | 600 tests × 6 runs |
| 10.5.10 | Browser tests; file changes | 600 tests × 6 runs |
| 10.5.7 | Browser tests; `r` key | 600 tests × 6 runs |
| 10.5.7 | Browser + one Node test; `r` key | 601 tests × 6 runs |

### Report size and memory

With 160 DOM rows per story, both configurations completed 600 tests × 3 runs.

| Measurement | Full reports | Explicit `resultTypes` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Observed Node heap peak (MiB) | 2,460.17 | 273.59 |
| Final Node heap after GC (MiB) | 788.74 | 140.03 |
| Sample report size (bytes) | 903,502 | 40,845 |

This comparison used the configuration workaround, rather than a PR build. Both configurations passed. Heap peaks are sampled and exclude Chromium.

### Remaining limits

- The reporter's exact command, rerun method and project have not been matched. The CLI checks above did not reproduce their OOM.
- Disabling IPC history reduced retained reports, but the old 10.5.10 managed runner still had long completion times. Later payload reductions are already in this PR's base.
- Vitest Node forks also use advanced IPC. The partial `ValueDeserializer` stack alone does not identify the reporter's process path.
- Stable parent heap after GC does not establish stable RSS or memory use across all processes.

### Environment and measurement notes

| Experiment | Environment |
| --- | --- |
| Published versions | macOS arm64; Node 25.9.0; Vitest 4.1.10; Vite 7.3.6; axe-core 4.14.0 |
| PR checkout | macOS arm64; Node 24.3.0; axe-core 4.11.0 |

Compare before/after within each experiment. The absolute values are not a version-to-version benchmark.

Earlier API controls used one worker and forced GC after each run. The CLI checks above used default concurrency and no GC between runs.

### Earlier component measurements

Custom standalone reporters that need full passing-node details can set `parameters.a11y.options.resultTypes` explicitly. The existing payload reductions and crash recovery from #36436 remain in place.

The 200-row fixture used Node 24.3.0, axe-core 4.11.0 and Execa 9.6.1 on macOS arm64.

| Report measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| JSON bytes | 1,150,644 | 48,248 |
| Violation / incomplete nodes | 3 / 2 | 3 / 2 |

Violation and incomplete nodes had the same serialized content. A separate IPC probe sent repeated report copies to isolate retention; it did not run 600 stories.

[Earlier component scripts and samples](https://gist.github.com/solp721/1b45e49f610882c9865e2330a8121bb7). That gist predates the repeated-run experiments above and does not contain their new logs or figure.


### Direct IPC retention check

After three 30-story runs on 10.5.7, Execa's returned `ipcOutput` contained:

| Measurement | Before | With IPC buffering disabled |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Retained IPC messages | 79 | 0 |
| Retained completed-run payloads | 3 | 0 |
| Messages received by parent | 79 | 79 |

All tests passed. The 79 messages include three measurement messages. Disabling buffering removes stored history; message deserialization and delivery still occur.

</details>

AI disclosure: developed with Claude Code and Codex assistance under my direction.

Focused local checks on Node 24.3.0 and Vitest 5.0.3:

- **A11y:** 20 tests passed across four files. Hook tests cover the standalone default, explicit settings and unchanged input parameters. A real-axe test checks reduced passing-node details and preserved violations.
- **Boot runner:** 35 tests passed, including the `buffer: { ipc: false }` option assertion and existing crash/restart tests.

These checks used a local test setup, not the full repository CI environment. Full sandbox E2E and manager UI QA have not been completed.

fix(import): stop reading other browsers' data before an import

## What and why

On a recent macOS, opening Signet showed "Data Access Blocked: Signet tried to access your data from other apps", and Signet ended up listed under System Settings › Privacy & Security › Files & Folders › Signet › Google Chrome, turned off.

macOS now protects other browsers' data. To decide what to offer in the import lists (welcome screen, Settings › Import, command bar), Signet listed the `Extensions` folder of the Chrome profile, without the user asking for anything. Checked on macOS 27 from the app itself:

| Operation on `~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| check that a file or folder exists | allowed |
| list a folder | `EPERM`, alert |
| read a file (Bookmarks, Preferences), copy History | `EPERM` |

Changes:

- `profileHas` only checks that files exist (the `Extensions` folder included): nothing is read or listed before the user imports.
- `extensionIds` reports a denied access instead of returning "no extension".
- When an import is denied on macOS, Signet explains where to allow it (Files & Folders › Signet › <browser>) with a button that opens that settings pane, in English and French.

## How I tested it

- Probed the operations above from the built app (launched with `open`, so macOS attributes the access to Signet).
- New unit tests: an `Extensions` folder that can't be listed (`chmod 000`) is reported as present by `profileHas`, and `extensionIds` throws instead of returning nothing.
- Built the app and launched it with an empty profile (welcome screen, import sources listed).

- [x] macOS
- [ ] Linux
- [ ] Windows
- [ ] iOS
- [ ] Android

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run i18n:check` and `npm test` pass
- [x] `npm run test:e2e` passes, or the change doesn't touch the desktop app
- [x] New visible text exists in English and French
- [x] macOS-only APIs are guarded (`IS_MAC`, `windowChrome()`)
- [x] Tests added or updated where it makes sense
- [ ] Manual checks added to `docs/A-VERIFIER.md` if the change can't be tested automatically

+import { chmodSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs'
+import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
+import { join } from 'node:path'
+import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
+import { extensionIds, profileHas } from './chromium'
+
+let profile: string
+beforeEach(() => {
+  profile = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'signet-chromium-'))
+})
+afterEach(() => {
+  const extensions = join(profile, 'Extensions')
+  if (existsSync(extensions)) chmodSync(extensions, 0o755)
+  rmSync(profile, { recursive: true, force: true })
+})
+
+/** An Extensions folder that can't be listed, like another browser's profile protected by macOS. */
+function lockedExtensions(): void {
+  mkdirSync(join(profile, 'Extensions', 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa'), { recursive: true })
+  chmodSync(join(profile, 'Extensions'), 0o000)
+}
+
+// Windows has no such permissions, and root ignores them: the test would prove nothing there.
+describe.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32' || process.getuid?.() === 0)('Chromium profile protected by the system', () => {
+  it('profileHas only checks that files exist: it lists nothing and does not fail', () => {
+    lockedExtensions()
+    expect(profileHas(profile)).toEqual({ history: false, passwords: false, extensions: true })
+  })
+
+  it('extensionIds reports the denied access instead of "no extension"', () => {
+    lockedExtensions()
+    expect(() => extensionIds(profile)).toThrow(/EACCES|EPERM/)
+  })
+})
+
+describe('extensionIds', () => {
+  it('no Extensions folder, or an empty one: no extension', () => {
+    expect(extensionIds(profile)).toEqual([])
+    mkdirSync(join(profile, 'Extensions'))
+    expect(extensionIds(profile)).toEqual([])
+  })
+})

fix(updates): check for updates in the installed app

## What and why

In the installed app, Help › Check for Updates always said "Couldn't check for updates", and the automatic checks failed silently. Signet loaded electron-updater with `import()`, and in the built app its `autoUpdater` is only reachable through `default` (it's a CommonJS getter): the named export was `undefined`, so the check threw before reaching GitHub.

`Updates.load` now reads `default.autoUpdater` first. The unit test mock now has the same shape as the built app, so this can't slip through again.

Version 0.1.0 is affected: it can't find updates by itself.

## How I tested it

Built the app (`electron-vite build`, then `electron-builder --mac zip --arm64`) and ran it with an empty profile. The automatic check, 30 seconds after launch, now reaches the published v0.1.0 release:

```
Checking for update
Update for version 0.1.0 is not available (latest version: 0.1.0, downgrade is disallowed).
```

- [x] macOS
- [ ] Linux
- [ ] Windows
- [ ] iOS
- [ ] Android

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run i18n:check` and `npm test` pass
- [x] `npm run test:e2e` passes, or the change doesn't touch the desktop app
- [x] New visible text exists in English and French (no new text)
- [x] macOS-only APIs are guarded (`IS_MAC`, `windowChrome()`)
- [x] Tests added or updated where it makes sense
- [ ] Manual checks added to `docs/A-VERIFIER.md` if the change can't be tested automatically

Closes #132

## 1. Өдөрт нэг удаа
Өнөөдрийн хичээл амь зарцуулдаггүй тул давтаад хязгааргүй оноо, XP авах боломжтой байсан. Local дээр 8 удаа давтахад оноо +240 болж, амь хөдлөөгүй.

- `GAME.REVIEW_PER_DAY = 1`: хичээл бүрт өдөрт нэг удаа.
- Өнөөдөр дуусгасан review байвал `REVIEW_DONE` (409) буцаана: "Өнөөдрийн хичээлээ хийчихлээ. Маргааш дахин ирээрэй".
- Зэрэг ирсэн хүсэлт давхар үүсгэхгүйн тулд мөн нөхцөлийг `INSERT` дотор дахин шалгана.

## 2. Асуулт сонгох query
Өмнө нь нэг `OR q.id IN (...)` нөхцөлтэй, `tier` шүүлтгүй байсан тул `questions` хүснэгтийг бүтнээр уншдаг байв. Одоо хоёр хэсгийг `UNION`-оор нийлүүлнэ:
- хичээлийн хуудасны асуулт (`tier`, `subject` шүүлттэй);
- хүүхдийн тэр хичээл дээр өмнө бодсон асуулт.
